# Chart

A picture of numbers: comparison, trend, share or spread.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Totals over time on dashboards.

- **Use it when:** The story is a relationship in a set of numbers, not a single number.
- **Not when:** A table is clearer, the set is too small, or the chart is decoration.

Instead:

- [Table](./table.md): The numbers as rows; often needed beside the chart.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A number in a table</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> type.data</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> type.body</div></div><div class="cap">Mono digits line up in columns, so values compare at a glance.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The same numbers are available as a table or text; color is not the only key. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add chart
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Chart reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.
